identification.summary: Storm-1607 is a Microsoft threat actor designation. Microsoft describes it as the actor behind email campaigns in which Microsoft first observed the ClickFix social-engineering technique, between March and June 2024 [S1]. A secondary source (not cited) also lists it among actors using Lumma Stealer; this was not confirmed in the Microsoft post [S2].
identification.firstObserved: March-June 2024 (Microsoft's first observation of ClickFix in Storm-1607 email campaigns) [S1].
identification.notes: No aliases are stated by any source gathered, so none are added. Do not merge with Storm-0426, Storm-0249 or Storm-1877, which Microsoft tracks separately as ClickFix-related actors [S1].

targeting.notes: Microsoft names US and Canadian organizations as targets of a May 2024 campaign of tens of thousands of emails and names no sectors [S1].

capabilities.summary: Mass phishing email with HTML attachments (example file name pattern reports_528647.html) using payment and invoice lures. The HTML mimics a Word document with an error dialog and a 'How to fix' button that copies a malicious command to the clipboard and instructs the victim to paste it into Windows Terminal (ClickFix). The goal was to install DarkGate, a commodity loader capable of keylogging, cryptocurrency mining, C2 communications and downloading additional payloads [S1]. A secondary report (unverified against the Microsoft text) also lists the actor among Lumma Stealer users [S2].

campaigns.name: First observed ClickFix email campaigns
campaigns.summary: Microsoft first observed ClickFix in email campaigns sent by Storm-1607, with HTML attachments that attempted to install DarkGate [S1].

campaigns.name: Payment/invoice lure campaign against US and Canada
campaigns.summary: A campaign of tens of thousands of emails targeting organizations in the United States and Canada, using payment and invoice lures [S1].

campaigns.name: Listed among Lumma Stealer users
campaigns.summary: Unconfirmed: a secondary report lists Storm-1607 among actors using Lumma Stealer per Microsoft's analysis; the Microsoft text was not directly verified.

diamond.adversary: Unattributed actor; sponsor, nationality and motivation not stated in sources [S1].
diamond.capability: ClickFix phishing lure via HTML attachment, DarkGate loader, Lumma Stealer use [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: No domains, IPs or hashes published in the sources gathered [S1].
diamond.victim: Organizations in the United States and Canada (May 2024 campaign); sectors not stated [S1].
diamond.technology: Email delivery of HTML attachments and user-executed clipboard-pasted commands in Windows Terminal; relies on user action rather than a software vulnerability [S1].

gaps: Sponsor, motivation (criminal vs other) and any relationship to other Microsoft-tracked ClickFix actors are not stated in the sources gathered.
Activity after 2024 is not documented in the sources gathered beyond a single Lumma Stealer mention [S2].

No sectors, infrastructure, indicators or final payload outcomes (for example ransomware) were found; the Lumma blog's exact characterization of the actors listed was not independently confirmed beyond the fetched summary.
Microsoft's Threat Intelligence ClickFix report listing and any MITRE ATT&CK group entry were not found; no MITRE group ID exists in the record.
A secondary article grouping Storm-1607 with other ClickFix actors surfaced in search but was not opened or verified.
Microsoft's naming mapping file was not confirmed as listing Storm-1607 and was removed as a source.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1-2: Corporate email gateways and user endpoints with Windows Terminal or PowerShell access are the relevant terrain; the technique depends on user action [S1]. STEP 3: Observed template is bulk email, HTML attachment, fake Word error, clipboard-pasted command, DarkGate loader [S1]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued commodity-malware phishing against North American organizations; MDCOA (not supported by sources, offered only for planning) would be use against defense-adjacent mailboxes. Candidate indicators: inbound HTML attachments with payment or invoice themes, user-launched Windows Terminal or PowerShell commands following browser activity, and DarkGate or Lumma Stealer detections [S1][S2].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track Microsoft ClickFix and commodity-loader reporting for email-borne activity [S1]. (2) Authorities and mission assurance: restricting user execution of pasted commands and blocking HTML attachments are local enterprise decisions; confirm with the system owner. (3) Coordinate: share indicators through established DoD and DIB reporting channels. The sources do not tie this actor to state activity, so treat as a criminal-style threat unless later evidence changes this.
